<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="כסלו_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518915304_theRebbe_180" batchId="meluket-_D7_9B_D7_A1_D7_9C_D7_95_meluket__BH_POST_1766518915304_theRebbe_180__p001">
  <section v="0">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section provides the date and location of the discourse.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">With the help of Heaven.</t>
    <t s="1">Motzaei Shabbos Parshas Vayetzei,</t>
    <t s="2">the 9th of Kislev,</t>
    <t s="3">the eve of the 10th of Kislev – in his room – 5738*</t>
  </section>
  <section v="1">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section introduces the verse "And I will return in peace to my father's house" and raises several questions about its precise wording and sequence.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">"And I will return in peace to my father's house, etc."1</t>
    <t s="1">[This verse is the beginning of the first discourse of our parshah in Torah Ohr by the Alter Rebbe and in Toras Chayim by the Mitteler Rebbe, the Baal HaGeulah</t>
    <t s="2">(of Yud Kislev)2</t>
    <t s="3">and the Hillula</t>
    <t s="4">(of the 9th of Kislev).</t>
    <t s="5">However, in Toras Chayim he prefaces</t>
    <t s="6">(at the beginning of the discourse)</t>
    <t s="7">the verse3</t>
    <t s="8">"And Yaakov vowed a vow, etc." which precedes the verse "And I will return in peace, etc."],</t>
    <t s="9">And the precise points in this are known,</t>
    <t s="10">What is the meaning of his saying "And I will return in peace to my father's house,"</t>
    <t s="11">specifically "in peace"4.</t>
    <t s="12">And especially that before this3</t>
    <t s="13">he says "If G-d will be with me, etc. and give me bread to eat and clothing to wear,"</t>
    <t s="14">that the intention in this is also for bread and clothing in a spiritual sense5,</t>
    <t s="15">in all the interpretations of this,</t>
    <t s="16">and nevertheless he is not satisfied with this and emphasizes that his return to his father's house will specifically be in peace.</t>
    <t s="17">And also one must understand what after "And I will return in peace to my father's house" he adds "and HaVaYaH will be to me for a G-d,"</t>
    <t s="18">for this matter that HaVaYaH is the G-d is an essential and constant matter</t>
    <t s="19">(as explained in many places6),</t>
    <t s="20">and what is the novelty in the above</t>
    <t s="21">(and the elevation)</t>
    <t s="22">in "and HaVaYaH will be to me for a G-d"7,</t>
    <t s="23">and especially after "And I will return in peace to my father's house."</t>
    <t s="24">And also one must understand what is said afterwards8</t>
    <t s="25">"and this stone which I have set as a pillar shall be a house of G-d,"</t>
    <t s="26">how can it be that a stone, which is inanimate</t>
    <t s="27">[for even after all the elevations in it</t>
    <t s="28">(by means of "which I have set as a pillar")</t>
    <t s="29">it is still called a stone,</t>
    <t s="30">a level of inanimate]</t>
    <t s="31">will be on such a lofty level that it will be a house of G-d9.</t>
    <t s="32">And it is explained in the discourses10</t>
    <t s="33">that the explanation of "and HaVaYaH will be to me for a G-d" is that a higher light will be drawn down,</t>
    <t s="34">such that relative to this light,</t>
    <t s="35">HaVaYaH</t>
    <t s="36">(of now)</t>
    <t s="37">will be</t>
    <t s="38">(only)</t>
    <t s="39">a level of Elokim.</t>
    <t s="40">And the explanation of "and this stone, etc. shall be a house of G-d"</t>
    <t s="41">(which comes after and in continuation of "and HaVaYaH will be to me for a G-d")</t>
    <t s="42">is that the stone will be a house for the G-d that will be then,</t>
    <t s="43">for HaVaYaH that will be for a G-d.</t>
    <t s="44">Based on this, further explanation is needed as to how it is possible that the stone,</t>
    <t s="45">an inanimate object,</t>
    <t s="46">will be a house for this G-d.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="2">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the narrative of Yaakov's vow provides an eternal lesson and empowerment for every Jew, connected to the concept of "Vayetzei."</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">B)</t>
    <t s="1">Now, since the Torah is eternal11,</t>
    <t s="2">it is understood,</t>
    <t s="3">that the matter of "And Yaakov vowed a vow, etc." is a lesson for every single Jew in all places and in all times.</t>
    <t s="4">And moreover,</t>
    <t s="5">since "the deeds of the fathers are a sign for the children"12,</t>
    <t s="6">the lesson from the matter of "And Yaakov vowed a vow, etc." is</t>
    <t s="7">(like all the matters of the deeds of the fathers)</t>
    <t s="8">with greater intensity and greater strength.</t>
    <t s="9">[And from this it is understood,</t>
    <t s="10">that also the empowerment within this lesson is not merely a general empowerment,</t>
    <t s="11">like all lessons of the Torah</t>
    <t s="12">(which are also an empowerment13),</t>
    <t s="13">but a special empowerment,</t>
    <t s="14">since this lesson is from the deeds of the fathers,</t>
    <t s="15">and the deeds of the fathers are</t>
    <t s="16">(not only a sign,</t>
    <t s="17">but also)</t>
    <t s="18">an empowerment14</t>
    <t s="19">for the children].</t>
    <t s="20">And since "And Yaakov vowed a vow, etc." comes in continuation of "And Yaakov went out"15</t>
    <t s="21">from Be'er Sheva, etc.</t>
    <t s="22">[as is also understood simply,</t>
    <t s="23">that the request "And I will return in peace to my father's house" is related to "And he went out, etc."</t>
    <t s="24">For because he went out from Be'er Sheva</t>
    <t s="25">(and his father's house)</t>
    <t s="26">therefore he asked that he should return and go back there,</t>
    <t s="27">and that his return should be in peace],</t>
    <t s="28">it is understood from this,</t>
    <t s="29">that so too regarding the lesson for every single Jew from "And Yaakov vowed a vow, etc."</t>
    <t s="30">[and from the request "And I will return in peace to my father's house, etc."],</t>
    <t s="31">that this relates to the matter of "And he went out, etc. from Be'er Sheva" as it is in every single Jew.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
